RBS Citizen Bank Culture and Change Essay

Table of Contents
 1. Introduction
 2. Conclusion
 3. References

Introduction

RBS citizen bank started its operations in 1828 in “Providence, Rhode Island” with a minor community bank named “high street bank”. Currently, the financial group runs over “1,500 branches with 20,900 employees and 3,900 ATMs in 12 states” (Benioff & Adler, 2006). Attributable to its growth, RBS citizen moved from its position as the fifth largest within US smallest states to its current position. As such, it is among the 15 leading banking firms in the nation.

The culture of RBS citizen is evident in extraordinary skilled employees who stay in the organization whilst working tirelessly to elevate their ranks. The entity offers a steady environment for their employees to exercise and develop their skills. In addition, it maintains ethical standards such as integrity to safeguard its personnel, surrounding communities and customers. As the organization maintains its culture, it attains success (Benioff & Adler, 2006).

Organizational changes arise in different dimensions. Often, they become manifest in new and inexperienced technologies, reorganization, invention of different pay plans and introduction of new programs on performance consideration. A common effect of change in many organizations is denial amongst the affected employees. In the organization, employees shun changes since they them come as a surprise without warning thus threatening the balance of RBS citizen.

Secondly, RBS citizen employees shun changes due to misunderstanding or inadequate skills to tackle emerging challenges. Various changes that happen within the entity come without sufficient training thus, positive changes are often perceived in unconstructive ways by the employees.

Thirdly, shunning new changes among the employees is caused by inertia. Most employees of RBS citizen wish to preserve their safe, sure and secure status. Therefore, initiation of new ideas in the company is a contradiction of their norms. Common problems in the entity that result from inertia have their origin in the technological sector (Robbin, 2007).

Fourthly, resistance to change by employees in the entity arises from competing commitments. Occasionally, the employees are comfortable with the changes in their career but consider how changes will affect their attainment of other objectives. These force employees to shun reorganizations that could have culminated in positive changes in the organization.

In order to overcome the employees’ resistance to change, I will recommend the following alternatives. Firstly, it is paramount to conduct education and communicate aptly with the employees. When this strategy is applied, it will bring appealing results to RBS citizen since it supports correctional measures.

This method will help the employees to distinguish the real implication of change and facts behind it. The organization can effectively conduct education and communication through discussions amid the management and employees, publishing special reports on the concern and conducting official group presentations.

Secondly, RBS citizen should consider involving its employees in the design of new changes within the organization. Involvement and participation of employees in designing and implementing changes within the organization will neutralize irrational and rational fears generated by changes.

Thirdly, the entity should offer support to their employees once they establish the cause of opposition. Support comes from management team through counseling on job-related stress, offering special training to employees and reimbursement. This strategy will facilitate the RBS citizen employees to accept the productive changes. Fourthly, RBS citizen should negotiate and agree with its employees before bringing changes in the organization (Robbin, 2007).

In addition, the managers should employ and communicate information to employees in a manner that will enhance the acceptance of changes. Finally, when the RBS citizen management fails to apply the given strategies to their employees, they can use clear and unspoken coercion. Here, the management forces employees to accept changes through threatening to terminate, transfer and demote them.

Implementing change efforts in an organization is a challenging and serious task that assumes a dangerous twist with the increasing change rates in organizations. Many people seem to deny changes whether they are from in-house or external issues. In RBS citizen, implementing change efforts occurs through the implementation model entailing seven steps. Firstly, the entity considers and handles human concerns because they regard people as their utmost strength.

Therefore, during change efforts, RBS citizen takes time to understand how new changes will affect people. Secondly, RBS citizen applies its strong leadership in the change process because without it, constructive changes may fail to happen. In addition, its employees are committed to changes and work tirelessly to see it happen with the intent of acquiring their organizational objectives.

Thirdly, RBS citizen employees have faith in their leadership meaning that during organizational changes, they trust in positive results from such changes. Fourthly, RBS citizen undoubtedly articulates the company’s vision to personnel for improved understanding of its implications.

In accordance to this, the RBS citizen administration team explains to their employees the motive of the changes. Fifthly, RBS citizen creates a facilitating environment to all people by identifying possible barriers that could affect implementation process. Moreover, when the management team discovers that present silos block change implementations, they break them to enhance changes (McShane & Glinow, 2005).

In addition, the company celebrates success, which motivates the involved individuals thus driving positive messages. Finally, RBS citizen puts the already occurred changes in its culture, shared values and standards. This encourages its employees because culture does not change easily. This insinuates that if changes affect culture, they will be lasting (McShane & Glinow, 2005). However, the implementation of change within the entity is not effective since its efforts fail in addressing emerging concerns.

Conclusion

Change requires that people adjust thus they ought to acknowledge that the changes could lead to positive results. RBS citizen should comply with all their implementation efforts resulting in their employees viewing change in a different perspective. In addition, RBS citizen employees should act with great standards of integrity and ethics in their actions and decisions to enhance the entity’s success

Linguistic Relativity and Cognitive Science: Unpacking the Complexities of Language and Thought

Introduction

In recent years, scholars have been increasingly fascinated with the relationship between language and thought, particularly within the context of cognitive science. One theory that has gained significant attention is linguistic relativity, which suggests that the structure and vocabulary of our languages shape our perception, understanding, and expression of reality. This paper will delve into the intricacies of linguistic relativity and its implications for cognitive science, exploring both the supporting evidence and criticisms of this theory.

Understanding Linguistic Relativity

At its core, linguistic relativity posits that the words and grammatical structures we use in our daily communication influence how we think about and categorize objects, events, and experiences. Different languages offer varying ways of expressing similar concepts, leading researchers to wonder whether these differences might lead speakers down divergent cognitive paths. For instance, English speakers are more likely to use explicit nominalization - turning verbs into nouns - when discussing abstract concepts, while Chinese speakers tend to rely on phrasal constructions and metaphorical expressions (Kay & Kempton, 1984). Could such differences impact how each group conceives of these ideas?

One key proponent of linguistic relativity was Benjamin Lee Whorf, who argued that the categories and distinctions present in a given language reflect the speaker's "cultural experience" and affect their perception of reality (Whorf, 1956). He famously pointed out that Hopi, an indigenous American language, lacks a single word for "time," yet its speakers seem capable of perceiving time precisely without needing separate lexemes for past, present, and future tenses. Whorf hypothesized that the lack of emphasis on temporal distinction in Hopi might encourage speakers to view time differently than English speakers do.

Evidence Supporting Linguistic Relativity

Studies across various domains have offered support for linguistic relativity, suggesting that language may indeed play a role in shaping our thoughts and perceptions. In the realm of color cognition, for example, research has shown that speakers of different languages categorize colors differently based on their respective terminologies (Brown et al., 2017). Speakers of Guugu Yimithirr, an Australian Aboriginal language, employ multiple terms for subtly distinct shades of blue-green hues unmatched in other tongues. In contrast, Japanese features a singular term for all blues and greens. These findings coincide with studies demonstrating that Guugu Yimithirr speakers exhibit enhanced discrimination abilities among those same blue-green gradations compared to Japanese and English speakers (Gilbert et al., 2006; see also Frankfurt, 1983). Such results suggest that the linguistic nuances of Guugu Yimithirr may influence its speakers' visual perception and cognition.

Another area where linguistic relativity seems relevant is spatial reasoning. Research conducted by Spivey and colleagues revealed that speakers of cultures using cartesian coordinates (e.g., English) perform better at tasks requiring mental rotation compared to speakers of non-cartesian coordinate systems (Spivey-Knowlton et al., 1997). This finding supports the idea that linguistic frameworks shape our cognitive processes, including spatial representations. Additionally, investigation has found that the presence or absence of certain linguistic constructs related to space influences the way people navigate through physical environments (Tversky, 1993). For example, because many Indigenous languages lack a specific preposition indicating directionality, speakers of those languages rely more heavily on landmarks for navigation, whereas English speakers might rely more on mental maps referencing cardinal directions.

Criticism and Limitations

Despite the compelling evidence accumulated thus far, some critics argue that linguistic relativity oversimplifies the complex interplay between language and thought (DeKeyser, 2007). They point out that the correlation between language and cognition cannot be reduced solely to language; extralinguistic factors, such as culture, social norms, and individual experience, must also be considered. Furthermore, challenging cases exist where linguistic diversity does not yield expected cognitive consequences, casting doubt on the universality of linguistic relativity (e.g., Kay & Kempton, 1984). Other limitations include difficulties in isolating causality between language exposure and cognitive development (Kovacs & Mehler, 2017), as well as the confounding effects of sociocultural variables (Mufwene, 2008).

Future Directions and Implications

As research continues to advance, it becomes clear that addressing the shortcomings of previous work will require innovative approaches and expanded methodological toolkits. To adequately assess the relationship between language and cognition, researchers should consider the dynamic nature of language contact situations, where individuals exposed to multiple languages negotiate meaning and identity (Pujolar, 2018). Investigating the experiences of bilingual and multilingual populations will provide valuable insights into the complex interactions between language, thought, and cultural background. Another promising line of inquiry lies in the integration of computational models and corpus-based analyses to evaluate linguistic patterns and their potential cognitive underpinnings (Frankenberg, 2019). Doing so could allow for more fine-grained examinations of how linguistic features relate to cognitive processing.

Conclusion

Linguistic relativity remains a contentious debate within cognitive science, but the existing body of evidence points towards a strong connection between language and human cognition. While acknowledging the limitations and complexity of this relationship, embracing linguistic relativity offers exciting opportunities for advancing our comprehension of the human mind and its incredible capacity for adaptation and flexibility. By continuing to explore the intricate dance between language and thought, we may gain new perspectives on our own cognitive processes and ultimately foster greater empathy and understanding across diverse linguistic and cultural communities. Ultimately, the study of linguistic relativity reminds us that language is not merely a tool for communication, but a powerful instrument for shaping our very perception of reality itself.

In the heart of a dense, verdant forest, where the leaves whisper ancient secrets and the earth hums with a life of its own, there exists a realm that is untouched by the clamor and clang of human civilization. This is a place where the symphony of nature is composed by the rustling of leaves, the babbling of brooks, and the harmonious choir of wildlife. It is in this natural cathedral, beneath the towering emerald spires of the trees, that one can truly grasp the essence of existence, the interconnectedness of life, and the silent wisdom that permeates every living thing.

Imagine, if you will, a single tree within this forest. Not just any tree, but an ancient oak, its roots delving deep into the fertile soil, its branches reaching towards the heavens as if in silent supplication. This oak has stood sentinel over countless seasons, bearing witness to the cycles of life, death, and rebirth that characterize the natural world. Its bark is etched with the scars of time, each one telling a story of survival against the elements, of resilience in the face of adversity. The tree serves as a microcosm of the forest itself, a testament to the enduring strength and adaptability of nature.

But what is it about this tree, this singular entity amidst a sea of flora, that captures our imagination and compels us to look deeper? It is, perhaps, the realization that within its sturdy trunk and sprawling roots lies a history far greater than our own. The oak has been a silent observer to the passage of centuries, its existence predating the oldest human civilizations. It has provided shelter and sustenance to countless generations of creatures, from the tiniest insects burrowing into its bark to the majestic birds of prey nesting in its crown. The tree is more than a life form; it is a living legacy, a bridge between the past and the present, a reminder of the enduring beauty and complexity of the natural world.

To truly understand the significance of this tree, one must also consider the myriad relationships it fosters within the forest ecosystem. It is a hub of biodiversity, its presence enabling the existence of a diverse array of species. The acorns it produces feed squirrels and other rodents, which in turn become prey for larger mammals and birds. The hollows in its trunk offer refuge for owls and other cavity-nesting birds, while the shade it casts provides respite for the undergrowth and the creatures that dwell within it. Even in death, the tree continues to give life, its decaying form becoming a nourishing source for fungi and insects, which then recycle its nutrients back into the soil, perpetuating the cycle of growth and renewal.

The oak tree, with its complex web of life, serves as an allegory for the interconnectedness of all things. It reminds us that no being exists in isolation, that each of us is part of a greater whole, bound together by the invisible threads of ecology and symbiosis. In recognizing this, we begin to see that our actions, however small they may seem, have far-reaching consequences. The health of a single tree can influence the well-being of an entire forest, just as the choices we make as individuals can impact the broader tapestry of our communities and, ultimately, the planet.

As we ponder the oak's place within the forest, we are also called to reflect on our own position within the world. Are we caretakers of the earth, nurturing its resources and preserving its wonders for future generations? Or are we mere passersby, indifferent to the delicate balance that sustains all life? The tree, in its silent wisdom, challenges us to consider our legacy, to contemplate what we will leave behind long after we are gone.

In this way, the tree becomes more than a symbol of nature's majesty; it becomes a mirror, reflecting our deepest values and aspirations. It asks us to look beyond the superficial trappings of our existence and to find meaning in our connection to the world around us. It invites us to slow down, to breathe deeply of the fragrant air, to listen to the quiet murmur of the forest and, in doing so, to rediscover a sense of wonder and reverence for the intricate dance of life.

In conclusion, the ancient oak in the heart of the forest stands as a monument to the enduring beauty and complexity of the natural world. It is a reminder of our shared history, of the intricate web of relationships that bind us to all living things, and of the responsibility we bear to safeguard this precious legacy. As we navigate the challenges of our time, let us draw inspiration from the strength and resilience of the oak, and strive to live in harmony with the earth, for in its fate lies our own.

Assassination of Osama Bin Laden Influence Synthesis Essay

Introduction

The death of Osama Bin Laden on mid-2011 by the US forces in Pakistan was received with minimal global opposition. The killing of the Al-Qaeda leader was a major step towards the fight against terrorism.

The following is a literature review on how the assassination of Osama Bin Laden was an example of how intelligence can make a real contribution to the international justice and the ‘rule of law’.

This paper presents the rule of law as the permissible code of rulings that administrate a country and not the subjective pronouncements by key government representatives.

On the other hand, international law will be presented as the set of policies that are universally acknowledged as obligatory when it comes to addressing affairs within and among countries.

Literature Review

Issues raised after Bin Laden’s Assassination

In his speech to the US House of Representative Judiciary Committee, the US Attorney General, Eric Holder stated that the action of the US Navy Seal of assassinating Osama Bin Laden was within the tenets of law. Confirming the same claims, Hasian (2012) and Krech (2011) say that the move was a national self-defence on a military target.

Holder presents Bin Laden’s butchery as a kill-or-capture mission and that since he (Bin Laden) had defied orders to be apprehended, the Navy Seals were justified to kill him.

From another perspective, Dahl (2014) reveals how the acumen that led to the death of Osama bin Laden shed a light on the importance of intelligence with respect to global justice and the rule of law.

Osama Bin Laden and his Al-Qaeda group were held accountable for several terrorist attacks across the world, particularly the 9/11 attack in the US. In their view, King, Glascock, and Levitt (2014) assert that counterterrorism measures have been more intelligence-oriented.

Inkster (2011) presents a clearer picture of the situation when he reveals the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) as among various intelligence agencies, which have created networks across the globe.

Although the agreement is not mutual, most commentators have agreed that the intelligence agencies have helped to attain global harmony and the rule of law as required by the United Nations Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy (UNGCTS).

According to Wachtel (2005), the UNGCTS has called members to enhance and enforce human rights and the rule of law when creating and executing counter-terrorism policies.

The Rule of Law and Osama’s Assassination

One of the basic principles of the rule of law is that all citizens or governments should be treated equally. Even criminals and terrorists should be treated under the same law.

In Oden’s (2007) view, terrorism hinders the enjoyment of human rights, demeans civil society, causes insecurity, and tampers with the socioeconomic development of victimised countries.

Thus, under the rule of law, countries should adopt counterterrorism measures to avert terrorism, apprehend, and prosecute suspects through a fair trial process. Presenting a similar opinion, Rollins (2011) says that countries should ensure that counterterrorism efforts are consistent with international laws.

Legal commentators such as Osborn (2011) and Rolins (2011) have held a contrary opinion that the targeted killing of Osama Bin Laden was unlawful and that it defied the tenets of human rights and international justice because the Navy SEAL had option to apprehend him when he was unarmed.

Such legal experts consider it as an act extrajudicial killing. In their move to counter Osborn (2011) and Rolins’ (2011) position, law experts such as Dahl (2014), Chiesa and Greenwalt (2012), and Ellmann (2007) clarify how the international law permits a country under the principle of Jus ad Bellum to apply force as a means of self-defence against military invasion if the United Nations Security Council authorises it.

The Al-Qaeda group had declared a holy war against America. It attacked its embassies in Africa and the World Trade Centre. Thus, the US forces were justified to go to Afghanistan and Pakistan in an effort to protect themselves from the armed attacks of the terrorist movement (Ellmann 2007).

Based on the reasoning of the supporters of Bin Laden’s killing, since the UN members are sovereign, they are required to respect the boundaries of other countries. However, in an attempt to protect its citizens from armed attacks, the US was authorised to attack Bin Laden, even in a foreign country (Rogers & McGoldrick 2011).

In Dumounchel’s (2012) view, whether a state should invade another country in pursuit of its enemy is determined by how the host country is cooperating. CIA had reported that Bin Laden resided close to the city, yet the Pakistan administration was not making efforts to arrest him.

The failure of Pakistan to collaborate with the international community to fight terrorism gave a room for the intercontinental neighbourhood to intervene (Lee 2014).

Osborn (2011) and other legal commentators who oppose the assassination assert that the Navy SEAL should have apprehended Bin Laden was both unrealistic and needless.

However, Dumounchel (2012) contends that the Al-Qaeda leader had become an enemy combatant and that based on the provisions of the international law, the US had a room to assault and assassinate him because one is allowed to confront his or her foe in a battlefield.

Arresting him would have been difficult. The US could not tell whether he had explosives or not since he was a terrorist. Moreover, detaining him would have been countered with brutal actions across the globe to instigate his release (Cerone 2011).

The Contribution of the Intelligence to Global Justice through Osama’s Targeted Killing

The intelligence work of the CIA that eventually led to the elimination of Bin Laden had various advantages, not only to the US but also to the global community. His assassination reinstated world peace.

The materials that were retrieved from the site revealed various plots that he and his counterparts had planned against America and its allies (Wong 2012). Moreover, considering that the attack and assassination were legal according to the international law, the Operation Neptune Spear that eliminated Bin Laden brought justice.

His death was justified for the many atrocities he had caused across the world (Lee 2014). The crimes he committed were indeed against humanity. Hence, as Alkana (2011) confirms, his demise was a stop to his heinous actions.

The UN is committed to fighting terrorism and retaining international peace. It has permitted members to ensure their national and global peace by creating and implementing counterterrorism policies (Paust 2011).

However, the UNGCTS calls for the creation of policies, which observe the rule of law whilst achieving international justice (Price 2011). As one of the means of countering terrorism, intelligence faces criticism with respect to how it contradicts with the principles of the rule of law.

Most intelligence strategies are seen to be torturous and contrary to the international human rights. It is important for intelligence agencies to stick to the rule of law when dealing with terrorists to ensure justice for the victims and suspects (Price 2011).

Conclusion

The discussion in this paper has considered a literature review on the death of Osama bin Laden with a focus on how it has contributed to the rule of law and global justice.

It has shown that the killing of Bin Laden was legal according the international law. Moreover, considering that he was responsible for several deaths and global uproar, his assassination brought global justice.

Once upon a time in a land far, far away, there lived a young girl named Eliza. She lived in a small village surrounded by dense forests and rolling hills. Her days were filled with the simple pleasures of life: playing with her siblings, helping her parents on their farm, and exploring the lush countryside that surrounded her home.

One day, while wandering through the woods, Eliza stumbled upon a hidden clearing. In the center of the clearing sat an ancient oak tree with a small door carved into its trunk. Intrigued, Eliza carefully knocked on the door, and to her surprise, it slowly creaked open to reveal a world unlike anything she had ever seen.

Inside, Eliza discovered a magical kingdom filled with talking animals, mystical creatures, and a friendly community of humans who had been granted the ability to speak with animals. The creatures welcomed her with open arms, and Eliza found herself embraced by this newfound family.

Over time, Eliza became known for her ability to understand and communicate with animals, using her gift to help the kingdom's creatures solve problems and live in harmony. She became a trusted advisor to the king of the kingdom, who often sought her counsel in times of crisis.

One day, the kingdom faced a great threat when a powerful sorcerer cast a dark spell over the land, causing the animals to lose their ability to speak. Eliza knew she had to act fast to find a way to break the curse.

She embarked on a perilous journey through the darkest depths of the forest, seeking the help of an enigmatic hermit rumored to possess the knowledge to undo the sorcerer's spell. After many trials and tribulations, Eliza finally found the hermit, who agreed to help her on the condition that she would deliver a precious gemstone from the heart of the enchanted forest to him.

With a heavy heart, Eliza agreed to the hermit's terms, knowing that the gemstone was guarded by a fierce dragon and that the journey would be fraught with danger. She set out on her quest, determined to save her newfound family from the sorcerer's curse.

Months passed as Eliza navigated the treacherous landscape, encountering many challenges along the way. At last, she reached the heart of the enchanted forest, where she found the dragon guarding the gemstone. The dragon, sensing the purity of Eliza's intentions, allowed her to take the gemstone and promised to accompany her on her journey home.

Returning to the kingdom, Eliza presented the gemstone to the hermit, who used it in a powerful ritual to break the curse and restore the ability to speak to the animals. The kingdom rejoiced as the animals regained their voices, and the sorcerer was vanquished, never to return.

Eliza had saved the kingdom and gained a deep respect from her new family. She knew that she would never forget the adventures she had experienced and the lessons she had learned in this magical realm. And so, with a heart full of gratitude, she returned to her village, ready to share the story of her incredible journey with her loved ones.

In a society where the risk of substance addiction is prevalent, it is crucial to understand the definition of a "hazardous" society and explore the policies in place to either engage in or prevent this issue. Additionally, it is vital to investigate the approaches that can mitigate the negative social impact on the individual affected by addiction.

In a hazardous society, the accessibility and acceptability of drugs and other substances are at alarmingly high levels. This can be attributed to various factors such as peer pressure, lack of education, and societal norms that may glamorize or romanticize substance use. In these environments, it becomes increasingly challenging for individuals to resist the temptation to engage in substance abuse, leading to potential addiction.

One policy that engages with the issue of hazardous societies is the implementation of strict regulations on drug distribution and sales. These regulations are designed to limit the accessibility of drugs, thereby reducing the likelihood of substance addiction. Moreover, public awareness campaigns and educational programs can play a significant role in informing people of the dangers associated with drug use and the importance of making informed decisions about their substance use.

However, prevention is not enough; it is equally crucial to address the negative social impact of substance addiction on the individual. In this regard, there are various approaches that can be taken to neutralize the adverse effects of addiction on the individual. One such approach is the provision of rehabilitation services and support groups for those struggling with addiction. These programs can help individuals overcome their addiction by offering them the necessary tools and resources to rebuild their lives and regain control over their substance use.

Another approach is the promotion of mental health and well-being as a means to prevent substance abuse in the first place. By addressing the root causes of addiction, such as stress, anxiety, and depression, individuals can learn to cope with life's challenges without resorting to substance use. This can be achieved through therapy, counseling, or other mental health interventions, which can be offered in schools, community centers, or healthcare facilities.

Lastly, fostering a culture of empathy and understanding can play a critical role in mitigating the negative social impact of addiction. By recognizing the struggles faced by those who suffer from addiction and offering support and encouragement, society can reduce the stigma surrounding substance abuse, thereby creating a more compassionate and inclusive environment for individuals in recovery.

In conclusion, it is essential to address the hazardous aspects of society that contribute to substance addiction. By engaging in policies that limit access to drugs and promoting awareness and education, we can help prevent the spread of addiction. Moreover, by implementing approaches that focus on the individual's well-being and offering support, we can neutralize the negative impact of addiction and create a more inclusive and empathetic society. Ultimately, these efforts will lead to a healthier, happier, and more supportive world for everyone.

Half a decade ago might as well have been yesterday, as my mind submerges into a pool of crystallized memories from those two months I spent in Peru. Every parent wants the best for their child, which is why mine decided to ship me 2500 miles away to study at a school during my precious vacation time. Through the eyes of a twelve-year-old, this idea seemed utterly ridiculous and unfair. However, I have come to understand the value behind this life-changing experience. My maturing eyes now witness the way in which it has provided me with a newfound sense of independence and a better appreciation of the education I receive. No longer will I be left defenseless, facing the fears and challenges that the impending future imposes; through this experience I have cultivated my weapon of preparation. Being on a plane for six hours and arriving in a foreign country without anyone but myself was terrifying. My parents' voices replayed through my head as their echoes reassured me that this was for my "own good." Although most of my family lived in Peru, where I was going was nowhere near their comforting presence. Thus, my challenge had begun. My original purpose for traveling to Peru was to enrich my knowledge and improve my Spanish, but I soon became aware of another motive: to overcome the fear of living without my parents. The head of the school was my aunt, which should have relieved some anxiety, except that she was a stranger to me. The emotional distress became so profound, I called my parents to demand my return home. Before I could say anything, however, my mother expressed how proud she was of me for doing this, with pure satisfaction ringing in her voice. I could feel the glow of her pride radiating from the phone; it was almost tangible. That was the moment I decided to stay and finish what I had started. Time really does heal all wounds because I grew to cherish this rewarding experience. I learned to take initiative for myself, such as cleaning my room, doing laundry, cooking, and working on homework, without being told to do so. My self-motivation and decision-making skills began to develop extensively from here. I also became devoted to my education and shortly realized it is a privilege, not a right. Living in a Third World country with poverty dominating the streets opened my eyes to an unfamiliar life where few educational institutions exist. I noticed this underprivileged society did not have the resources to reconstruct their country due to the lack of education, which helped me realize how powerful a tool it can be. Not only is education the key that will open most doors in the path of life, but also the basis for lifelong learning. My experience in Peru enabled me to acquire new responsibilities: as a student and an individual. It has given me a desire to seek knowledge for myself and fulfill my potential, ultimately preparing me for the beginning of this new chapter in my life.

The pressure of school is not limited to the academic year but extends into the summer as well. This is due to extracurricular activities and preparation for the forthcoming year, making summer a period of stress too. Across the United States, students are compelled to engage in summer projects aimed at reinforcing what they learned during the academic year. While this concept is logical, the design of these projects needs to be scrutinized. It is suggested that summer projects should be student-led to foster creativity and reduce stress. Although some might argue that this could compromise the learning experience due to lack of structure, it's important to have faith in every student's potential.

In the educational system, the majority of projects are designed by teachers. This is done to evaluate a student's skill set. However, introducing student-led projects could assist students in discovering their genuine interest in a subject and enhance their creativity. For example, when a student is required to conduct a science experiment on a specific wild plant, there is no room for creativity in choosing the subject of study. But, if students were allowed to select the plant and the experiment, it could enhance their creative thinking. This student-led project could also help students discover their love for science by exploring a plant that genuinely intrigues them. The argument for student-led summer projects is strengthened by the potential for increased creativity and innovation when students have the freedom to choose their study subject.

Stress is a common issue among students today. The pressure to meet teachers' expectations often leads to a negative attitude towards school. When a teacher assigns a project, what could have been an enjoyable learning experience can turn into a dreaded and stressful task. For instance, if a student is required to do a history project on Abraham Lincoln, they may view it as just another task to complete. However, if they were given the freedom to choose any president for their history project, they might find it enjoyable to research one of their favorite historical figures. This could be highly beneficial for the student as many students learn more effectively when they are not stressed about a specific objective. The absence of stress allows them to relax while still gaining valuable knowledge.

While summer projects are useful in ensuring that students retain information, they should not be teacher-led. Summer should be a period where students have the freedom to choose their projects, helping them discover their true interests. This can enhance a student's creativity by allowing them to engage in an activity they are genuinely interested in. Similarly, it can help students reduce stress by finding pleasure in their project.

The Dangers of Texting and Driving

In today's time, we all want to stay connected to our family, friends, and loved ones, now even more than ever. With the boom in technology and smart phones, it is no surprise that just about everyone has one. With those advances, we are able to keep in touch and stay connected with everyone by calling, sending emails, using social media, and by texting. Even though it may be easy and convenient to stay connected, and even though there are many other positive effects of technology, there also comes many negative effects are there comes great dangers to include texting and driving. There are both positive and negative effects when driving as well, when adding texting and other distractions in while driving, the negative effects, and dangers are increased a lot more. Calling and texting while behind the wheel has become increasingly common for many drivers in today's society, and just as it can become common, it has led to many distractions, more accidents, and more fatalities.

One cardinal rule of driving has always been to keep both hands on the wheel. While driving, even with the car on cruise control, sometimes we forget how much of a risk we are taking as we are not only responsible for our car, we must stay protected and cautious of those around us as well. Even though we only think of the temporary satisfaction or benefit that we have from driving, we often don't think of how we put ourselves, other drivers, and pedestrians at risk. Driving requires a lot of focus and it requires our full and undivided attention. Texting and driving places you at risk because you are taking your eyes off the road, you are taking your hands off of the wheel, and evening more you are taking your mind off of driving. Distractions such as texting or even calling can cause some of the smallest or some of the most life threatening, life altering issues. It is no surprise that texting while driving takes your concentration off the road and with the distractions, even for a second, it could have consequences some minor, while others can bring on serious consequences. With just a second of texting, we can miss important signs or messages on the road, it can lead to speeding which can lead to very expensive tickets. In addition to speeding fines and tickets, distracted driving also leads to higher insurance premiums which add up to be a lot over time. To some, that risk may be minor, but another serious consequence for distracted driving is that it can lead to jail time. It does not matter how good of a driver you may think you are or how good your driving skills may be, unless you are capable of equally concentrating on multiple things at one time (which is not possible), you will be distracted when doing anything other than focusing on the road, and that places you and others at a serious risk.

Accidents on the road can happen and anytime and for a number of reasons, but it is no surprise that if texting and driving leads to more distractions, those distractions also leads to more accidents and more fatalities. Over the years, as technology has advanced and with more ways to stay connected, combined with people that refuse to make the right decision, the rates and statistics of texting related deaths have drastically increased. While checking messages and emails, making phone calls, or even sending the shortest message, so many things can go wrong. Just the slightest distraction can cause someone to run off the road causing them to run off the road, hit another car, or even hit a pedestrian, Those distractions combined with high speeds, a tiny click of the finger can cause many to be critically injured or it can cause someone to lose their life. According to Luke Ameen, 1 out of every 4 car accidents in the United Stated are caused by texting and driving, 421,000 are injured in car crashed that have involved a driver who is distracted in some way, and 37,000 people die in auto accidents every year due to being distracted or texting while driving and those numbers are expected to increase over the years. Texting or reading a message takes your eyes off the road for a minimum of three seconds and within those short seconds someone can lose their lives or sustain life threatening injuries that they would have to live with for the rest of their lives. Even if all of those drivers are not at fault, they could have probably avoided the accident if they were not distracted by texting.

In an effort to reduce the number of accidents and fatalities caused by distracted drivers, people can take simple steps to help save lives. Although auto accidents take place every day and for a variety of reasons, distractions seem to cause more of a problem so if we limit or stop the distractions we can prevent accidents and help to save more people. While driving it is important for people to save the distractions for later. People have been encouraged to put their phones on silent or to turn them off, they can put their phones out of their reach such as in the glove compartment, back seat, or their trunks, or they can take other measures such as downloading apps that would prevent them from using the phone when it has been detected that their vehicles are in motion. While these are just a few things that can be done, people should do what is best for them. While these actions may seem extreme to some, saving their life or the lives of others is more important. Most states and insurance companies have also put policies and other actions in place that will assist with reducing the number of fatalities causes by texting or distracted driving. Most states have provided discounts for safe drivers while other states are issuing fines and some go to the extreme of jail time if drivers are caught texting or using their phones while driving. When driving, we are faced with enough dangers. Even though we want to stay connected to our friends, family, and loved ones, all it takes is a few seconds to never be able to get that opportunity again. While behind the wheels, taking simple actions can help save our life or the life of others. There are several options that we can take to cause an accident and just the same, there are several options that can be taken to prevent them from happening as well.

The influence of technology on human communication has been profound and far-reaching, transforming the way people interact with each other and exchange information. From social media platforms to instant messaging apps, digital technologies have revolutionized the way we communicate, creating new opportunities for connection and collaboration, but also posing challenges to traditional forms of communication and our ability to effectively communicate.

One of the most significant impacts of technology on human communication is the rise of social media. Social networking sites such as Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram have become an integral part of modern life, allowing users to connect with others across geographical distances and share their thoughts, experiences, and opinions. These platforms have created new communities and enabled people to form connections that might not have been possible before. For example, social media has allowed people who are geographically isolated or marginalized to find support and solidarity online, providing a platform for them to express themselves and engage with others.

However, social media has also had some negative effects on human communication. One of the main concerns is the loss of face-to-face interaction, which is essential for building strong relationships and effective communication. People are spending more time staring at screens and less time engaging in person-to-person interactions, leading to feelings of isolation and disconnection. Additionally, social media platforms often prioritize brevity over depth, encouraging short, superficial messages rather than thoughtful, well-crafted communications. This can lead to misunderstandings and miscommunications, as nuances and complex ideas are lost in translation.

Another area where technology has had a significant impact is in the realm of instant messaging. Apps like WhatsApp, WeChat, and Slack have made it easier than ever to send quick messages to friends, family, and colleagues. However, these platforms can also create expectations of immediate responses, blurring the boundaries between work and personal life. This can lead to burnout and stress, as people feel pressure to respond quickly, even when they need time to process their thoughts. Moreover, instant messaging can also contribute to the decline of written communication skills, as people rely more on abbreviations and emojis to convey their message, rather than taking the time to craft carefully considered sentences.

Furthermore, technology has transformed the way businesses communicate with customers. Email marketing, automated chatbots, and social media advertising have all become common strategies for reaching potential clients and promoting products or services. While these tools can be useful for increasing brand awareness and driving sales, they can also lead to spamming and overwhelming customers with too many messages. This can erode trust and loyalty, ultimately damaging the reputation of the company.

Moreover, technology has also affected the way we consume news and information. Online news sources and social media feeds have made it easier than ever to access breaking news and current events. However, this abundance of information can also lead to information overload, making it difficult to discern fact from fiction, and leading to confusion and mistrust. Furthermore, algorithms used by social media platforms can create echo chambers, where people only see information that confirms their existing beliefs, rather than being exposed to diverse perspectives.

In addition to these changes, technology has also influenced language itself. Emoticons, acronyms, and slang have become ubiquitous in digital communication, changing the way we express ourselves and understand each other. For instance, the use of "LOL" (laugh out loud) and "OMG" (oh my god) has become so widespread that they have become part of everyday speech. Similarly, the rise of emojis has added visual elements to communication, enabling people to convey emotions and tone more easily. However, these changes can also create barriers to understanding, particularly for older generations who may struggle to keep up with the latest trends and terminology.

Finally, technology has also had a profound impact on education and learning. Online courses and educational resources have democratized access to knowledge, allowing anyone with an internet connection to learn new skills and gain new insights. However, this shift towards digital learning has also led to concerns about the quality of education, as well as the potential for bias and manipulation in online content.

In conclusion, technology has had a profound impact on human communication, changing the way we interact with each other, exchange information, and express ourselves. While there are many benefits to these changes, including increased connectivity and access to information, there are also challenges to traditional forms of communication and our ability to effectively communicate. As technology continues to evolve, it will be important to consider these implications and work towards finding solutions that promote healthy communication, both online and offline. By doing so, we can ensure that technology serves as a tool for enhancement, rather than detriment, to our ability to communicate and connect with one another.

“Failure to Connect – How Computers Affect Our Children’s Minds and What We Can Do About It” by Jane M. Healy Essay

The modern world witnesses wide use of technology which assists in different kinds of processes people are involved into. The book “Failure to Connect – How Computers Affect Our Children’s Minds and What We Can Do About It” by Jane M. Healy deals with the assistance of technology in children’s learning process and the effects the technology produces on their minds. The book describes stages of children’s cognitive development as well as measures which should be taken by parents in order to “optimize their children’s mental growth” (Healy, 2000). Detailed analysis of several chapters of the book will help to understand the impact of computer technologies on children’s health and mental development.

To begin with, chapter 4 of the book deals with the impact of video games on children’s mental health. The author of the book advises parents to “(b)e alert for abnormally “spaced-out” behavior that can signal rare video-game-related seizures” (Healy, 2000). Indeed, these days most of children are obsessed with videogames. It has been proved that video games cause addiction which leads to children being abnormally dependent on them. It seems that the only way out for parents in case of their child’s dependence on video games is to choose those games which “encourage reading and original problem-solving instead of memorizing procedural routines” (Healy, 2000).

In addition, chapter 5 deals with learning environment and learning conditions of children. Healy emphasizes that “children who learn in one medium (screen vs. page) will always be inclined to prefer the one in which they learned” (Healy, 2000). From this it can be concluded that children who got used to studying by means of books are unlikely to have the same level of academic achievements when studying by means of computer. This happens due to a particular frame of the perception of information by a child for whom it is easier to comprehend the text written on the paper, rather than the one which appears at the screen.

Chapter six explores the impact of computer technologies on children’s health. It has been discovered that “some uses of computers can trigger hormonal changes that raise blood pressure or affect the immune system” (Healy, 2000). This is especially harmful for the health of children, since even the adults’ brain “is very responsive to small alterations in the hormonal system” (Healy, 2000). Negative effect of computer technologies on children’s health has been known for decades. Hormonal changes, raised blood pressure, and weakening of immune system may result in child’s serious problems with health in future. This being the reason, the time which the child spends using the computer should be limited.

In chapter 7 Healy states that “(p)reschoolers and even six- to eight-year-olds in no way need computers” (Healy, 2000). It is hard to disagree with her, since children at that age mostly use computers for fun, rather then for studying. Computers are more important for older children, though again, their usage for entertainment should be restricted.

Chapter 8 continues developing the idea presented in chapter 7. It describes the influence of computer technologies on preschoolers and children younger than eight years old. It turns out that using computers affects not only children’s physical health but “can “scaffold” [their mental] development” (Healy, 2000). Therefore, children should be allowed to use computers only for study purposes.

Finally, chapter 9 deals with a computer as “a “thinking” or “reasoning” substitute for human intelligence” (Healy, 2000). Indeed, computers facilitate a number of human activities and make people’s life easier. However, they will never be able to substitute for human intelligence for they are devoid of feelings and emotions being able to perform only a limited set of activities they have been programmed for.

References

Healy, J. (2000). Failure to Connect: How Computers Affect Our Children’s Minds–For Better and Worse . Simon & Schuster.

The Entrapment in Criminal Law Essay

Table of Contents
 1. History of entrapment as a defense
 2. Objectivity test for entrapment
 3. Different drug
 4. Reference

History of entrapment as a defense

According to Scheb (2010), entrapment is viewed as the inducing of a person to commit a crime. Basically, it is trapping a criminal into committing a crime as a means of gathering criminal evidence against the defendant. However, entrapment can also be used as a defense by the suspect. From this perspective, the law views that the defendant was coerced or was induced into getting into a criminal act that was not initially intended. Therefore, entrapment can only be deemed to be a defense, if the accused was innocent or was a suspect who never intended to act in the crime (Scheb, 2010). Moreover, entrapment is treated as a defense, if the act of crime was initiated by the government through its agents. In addition, entrapment can be a defense if the government agents created an opportunity for the crime to be executed by aiding and persuading the defendant. For the entrapment case to be used as a defense, the defendant should not have exhibited the intent of committing a crime prior to the entrapment (Scheb, 2010).

Entrapment was initially used by governments to nub criminals dealing in drugs and illegal arms. In most cases, the undercover officers use entrapment to prosecute criminals. The most prolific landmark case that brought entrapment into the limelight was first evidenced in the year 1864 in the United States. During this period a judge in the United States rejected the use of entrapment as a defense, arguing that this compromised the law. For example, issues related to the subjectivity and objectivity of the entrapment were raised. This evaluates whether the law enforcers use entrapment in an objective manner. On the other hand, the subjectivity of the entrapment evaluates whether the defendant intentionally committed the crime (Scheb, 2010).

In the case of Paula and Joseph, Paula used entrapment to arrest Joseph for possessing illegal drugs. Nonetheless, Paula’s use of entrapment does not pass the objectivity test considering that she further alleged to engage in sex with Joseph, if they used cocaine. In addition, Joseph who is the defendant had earlier declined Paula’s suggestions. However, the defendant did not possess cocaine, but marijuana. This indicates that his state of mind was predisposed to act in a criminal manner.

Objectivity test for entrapment

Most likely, Joseph’s case would be dismissed on the basis that he was not expecting to be entrapped by sex to commit a crime. At first, Joseph had declined and a further action by Paula to offer sex became tempting. Therefore, a state that objectively tests entrapment might dismiss the case. However, Joseph is unlikely to secure a dismissal of the case using entrapment as a defense. Although the objective was to arrest a cocaine drug dealer, Joseph produced another drug exhibiting his capability and intent to engage in criminal acts. This would not make any difference if the defendant committed a crime within a state that subjectively and objectively tests entrapment. As a person of sound mind, one should not commit acts of crime whether it is entrapment or not.

Different drug

Legally, the objectivity of the entrapment as used by Paula would change the case scenario. First, the objective was to arrest Joseph for possession of cocaine. However, cocaine and marijuana are categorized as illegal drugs and thus it makes no difference as to what drug was produced. As a matter of fact, Joseph had earlier agreed to bring cocaine with him, showing signs that he used drugs. Joseph produced a huge amount of marijuana a sign that he might also be involved in the selling of such drugs.

Reference

Scheb, M., J. (2010). Criminal law and procedure . Boston, MA: Cengage Learning.

There’s no person in the world that stays indifferent hearing the names of the sporting heroes. And now you can not only admire them, but you may also become a part of their world: Mike Finnigan, in his book They Did You Can , reveals the secrets of renowned athletes and shares the core issues which help achieve your goals.

The book caters for everybody who once tried to succeed in sports but, after experiencing some problems, gave up. Besides, it encourages the novices to put all their fears and take a challenge, prioritize and do their best to reach their objectives.

The key idea of the author is that “success is not about getting lucky. Failure is not about being unlucky. It is about you making things happen” (Finnigan 36). I can’t but agree with this evident statement. Personally, I tend to think it made me reassess my attitude towards life and my ambitions.

Eric Simons, former Coach of the South African Cricket Team, supports this idea: “success or failure will not be dependent on your ability to deal with the problem. It will depend on your attitude towards the problem“ (Finnigan 78).

Really beneficial seems to me the idea to provide interviews of successful people in sports as it could be a powerful motivation for aspiring athletes and just people who got disappointed in their abilities and are next to give up. Moreover, taking the initial step could be extremely frightening, so getting goals prioritized and abilities estimated is very supportive.

Inspiring and really helpful, the book made a great impact on me, bringing me to the thought of further self-development.

Finnigan, Mike. They Did You Can. Carmarthen, Wales: Crown House, 2007.

Influencing others is a common goal in many aspects of life, whether it be in personal relationships, professional settings, or even in public speaking. While there are many ways to influence others, I believe that setting a good example by your own behavior is the most effective way to do so.

When you set a good example by your behavior, you are demonstrating to others what you expect them to do. This can be particularly effective when you are trying to influence and direct people. For example, if you are a parent trying to teach your child a new skill, you will need to demonstrate the correct technique for them to follow. Similarly, if you are a teacher trying to teach your students a new concept, you will need to demonstrate how it can be applied in practice.

In addition to demonstrating the correct behavior, you will also need to provide good details to guide your audience. This can be particularly important when you are providing information to others. For example, if you are giving a presentation on a new product, you will need to provide details on its features, benefits, and how it can be used. Similarly, if you are writing a report, you will need to provide evidence and examples to support your arguments.

While setting a good example by your behavior is important, it is not the only way to influence others. Another way to influence others is by showing them in person. For example, if you are trying to learn a new skill, such as playing an instrument, you may need to watch someone else play in order to understand how it is done. Similarly, if you are trying to learn a new language, you may need to watch native speakers speaking in order to understand the correct pronunciation and grammar.

Overall, I believe that setting a good example by your own behavior is the most effective way to influence others. By demonstrating the correct behavior and providing good details to guide your audience, you can help others learn and grow. Additionally, by showing others in person, you can provide a more personal and interactive experience that can be particularly helpful for learning new skills.

The Film “Thirteen days” by Roger Donaldson Essay (Critical Writing)

The Cuban Missile Crisis

The Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962 encompasses confrontation based on the Soviet Union’s construction of nuclear missile bases in Cuba, with the United States on one side and Cuba as well as the Soviet Union on the other side. The Crisis began on October 14 and ended on October 28, 1962. The ensuing Crisis began when President John F. Kennedy saw the U2 spy plane surveillance photos, showing the Soviet Union’s construction of nuclear missile bases.

As a solution, the United States launched a quarantine to inspect all ships destined for Cuba. Nikita Khrushchev uses back-channel communication to indicate his willingness to remove the missiles as long as the US withdraws its invasion of Cuba by October 28. The Crisis ends with Kennedy’s agreement to withdraw Jupiter missiles in Turkey and Italy. These form the events of the Film “Thirteen days,” as directed by Roger Donaldson. Based on the fact that this is a political film, various political, environmental, social, and economic issues can be identified in the thirteen days that made up the Crisis.

The crucial political issues that occurred during this period include the construction of nuclear missile bases in Cuba by the Soviet Union, subversion of the peaceful solution being sought by President Kennedy, the death of one pilot during the cover-up of the antiaircraft shooting that O’Donnel ordered to foil Curtis LeMay’s idea of sending aircraft to Cuba, calling of military exercises in Puerto Rico to prepare for an invasion by General Maxwell Taylor, the loss of two Soviet Union ships and the shooting of one of the boats using aerial clusters as ordered by Admiral George Anderson, the Johnston Island’s ignition of hydrogen bombs and the dispatch and shooting down of a U-2 spy plane to Siberia.

The key environmental issues that occurred during the thirteen days encompass water pollution as caused by the American ships plying the Cuban waters during the Quarantine, ecological degradation due to the destruction of forest cover to give way to clear land to be utilized during the nuclear missile bases construction, resource depletion under which the production of the medium-range missiles by the Soviet Union depleted all natural resources and land degradation during the construction of the missile bases.

The significant Social issues that occurred during the thirteen days are inclusive of racism that the name red bastards bring out Nikita Khrushchev use of back-channel communication when communicating to the US president, the shuffling of counter offers and offers between the Soviet and American heads of the state increasing Third World War breakout fear, poor social relationships between America and the Soviet Union due to the construction of the missile bases by the Soviet Union and installation of Jupiter missiles in Italy and Turkey by the US, brinkmanship as well as the deviance shown by the military bosses when they made individual detrimental decisions without consulting the president.

The main economic issues that occurred during that period encompass increased energy use during the construction of the missile bases culminating into an energy crisis, creation of employment opportunities in the missile bases’ construction, offshoring as evidenced by the construction of the missile bases in Cuba rather than the Soviet Union, competitive behavior evidenced by the countering of the Soviet Union Missiles by the American missiles, war’s inefficiency puzzle and the economic calculation problem that faced Nikita Khrushchev on whether distribute more resources into the construction of the missile bases or to distribute resources equally in his economy.

President John F. Kennedy and special assistant Kenny O’Donnell

The two characters selected for this part include President John F. Kennedy and special assistant Kenny O’Donnell. Leadership encompasses the social influence process under which a person enlists the support of the help of other people in accomplishing a given task. Essentially, when he receives two mixed messages from the Soviet Union, he decides to respond to the message originating from Nikita Khrushchev with the aim of curbing an escalation in the already volatile situation facing the two countries. His dedication and commitment enable him to resolve the explosive problem peacefully. His commitment to this vision convinces the Soviet Union to seek a peaceful solution to the Crisis. He is competent due to his ability to identify the best solution, plan it, and implement it in such a way that he convinced his followers that he knew what he was doing.

For this reason, he removed Jupiter missiles in Italy and Turkey to ensure the removal of Missiles in Cuba by the Soviet Union. He is courageous and discerning as he is unwilling to appease the Soviet Union, which would accord them with the mandate to bully America into submission in the future. He is courageous enough to order a quarantine though he knew that this would escalate the volatile nature of the Crisis. Focus helps him to identify his priority of saving America by preventing the outbreak of a Third World War, and he concentrates on its achievement.

Kenny O’Donnell is a problem solver. This is because he accords the president with positive advice on the best course of action. Essentially, he foils General Curtis LeMay’s plan of escalating the Crisis by sending low-level reconnaissance planes into Cuba, which would be in turn shot down, culminating in military retaliation. He is charismatic because he thinks of others and their concerns before thinking about himself. In this case, the perceptibly explains the consequences of each proposed solution to the president to ensure that he makes the best choice.

This would, in turn, endear the president to the American though his leadership was facing considerable obstacles as the failed Bay of Pigs invasion. He is straight forward in the advice he accords the president. He is courageous because he subverted any escalation caused by the overzealous military bosses.
